description: Issue #867 (PR #884 cross-vendor review round 3): neutralizes RequestBindingPolicy.IsBannedGatewayType's open-generic dispatch (`if (banned.IsGenericTypeDefinition) { ... }`, src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Helper/RequestBindingPolicy.cs) with a compile-preserving `&& false` so every BannedGatewayTypes entry -- including the open generic ones (IOptionsMonitor<>/IOptionsSnapshot<>/IOptions<>) -- falls through to the plain `banned.IsAssignableFrom(memberType)` branch. This reproduces exactly the bug the review warned 'do not assume the open generic works' about: Type.IsAssignableFrom does not relate an open generic type DEFINITION to any of its closed constructions (typeof(IOptionsMonitor<>).IsAssignableFrom(typeof(IOptionsMonitor<Configs>)) returns false, pinned by RequestBindingPolicyTests867.OpenGenericTypeAssignability_ConfirmsIsAssignableFromDoesNotRelateOpenToClosedGenerics), so with this guard neutralized, IOptionsMonitor<>/IOptionsSnapshot<>/IOptions<> silently stop matching anything. Checked against IsPathAllowed_OptionsMonitorCurrentValue_ReturnsFalse ('Retention.CurrentValue.NormalDays', CurrentValue declared directly on IOptionsMonitor<T>), IsPathAllowed_OptionsValue_ReturnsFalse ('Opt.Value.NormalDays', Value declared directly on IOptions<T>), and IsPathAllowed_OptionsSnapshotBareSegment_ReturnsFalse (single-segment 'Snapshot' key). The Snapshot case is deliberately a BARE single-segment key, not a multi-segment one: IOptionsSnapshot<T> inherits Value from IOptions<T> rather than redeclaring it, and Type.GetMember on an INTERFACE does not walk up to base interfaces the way it does for classes (typeof(IOptionsSnapshot<ActionLogRetentionOptions>).GetMember("Value").Length == 0, verified empirically) -- so a 'Snapshot.Value.NormalDays' key is ALSO rejected by the independent zero-resolution guard regardless of whether this mutant is applied, which would make it a false positive for isolating this specific guard. The bare-segment key isolates hop 0 only, where IOptionsSnapshot<ActionLogRetentionOptions> itself must be recognized as a closed construction of the open generic IOptionsSnapshot<>. The green control, IsPathAllowed_ServiceProvider_ReturnsFalse, uses the fourth new entry (IServiceProvider, NOT generic) -- IsGenericTypeDefinition is already false for it, so this mutant's condition (`false && false`) has no effect on its code path and it must stay green, proving the mutant's blast radius is correctly scoped to the three generic entries only. A second green control (IsPathAllowed_SearcherDotCustomFilterField_ReturnsTrue) confirms the ordinary non-generic gateway-type checks (WTMContext/Configs/etc.) are also unaffected.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Helper.Request: must be rejected via IsOrImplementsOpenGenericDefinition at this single hop
must be rejected the same way as IOptionsMonitor
